about: Unicode text -> Shree-Lipi 7 Kannada bytes (fonts SHREE-KAN7-0850..0855/0899 = S0850890..S0855890/S0899890.TTF and Shree-Kan7-001/002 = WKAN7001/2.TTF; the 4/5/6 fonts SHREE-KAN-0850..0855/0899 = S08500F0..S08550F0/S08990F0.TTF have the same code set and identical glyphs), answered by Shree's own composers S8KanU64.dll (TutorGetMappedCodeW, Unicode) and S8Kan764.dll (TutorGetMappedCode, raw bytes) for the same keystroke. bytes = the 7 composer's raw output, one hex byte per glyph code (bytes 80-9F are raw bytes: in a document they sit on their Windows-1252 code points, except 8D and 90 which the fonts map at U+008D/U+0090; 80 81 8E 8F 9D 9E have no glyph). Every probe set and every vendor keyboard was captured twice in separate processes: byte-identical. kind: vendor-key = a key (layer 0, Ctrl+Space, or the composer raw code layer) of one of the 21 shipped .KAN keyboards loaded from its ORIGINAL path (the composers switch typing mode by name: ENG/PHONETIC/NEWROMA/ROMA/KGP* are phonetic); source names the keyboard, key and codes. canonical = probe in Shree's typing order for Kannada: the consonant (which the 7 composer writes with its talakattu head DC: ಕ = 50 DC), the nukta D3, then the vowel sign (which replaces or follows the head: ಕಾ = 50 DD, ಕಿ = 51 one glyph, ಕು = 50 DC E1, ಪು = B1 DC E2, ಕೆ = 50 E6, ಕೈ = 50 E6 E7, ಕೌ = 50 E8), the length mark 76 after ಿ ೆ ೊ (ಕೀ = 51 E0, ಕೇ = 50 E6 E0, ಕೋ = 50 E6 E3 E0), then the reph 4B (the arkavattu EC, struck AFTER its syllable: ರ್ಕಾ = 50 DD EC), then ಂ ಃ (ರ್ಕಾಂ = 50 DD EC ED); conjuncts through the link code 64 (C1 + head + the subjoined form of C2: ಕ್ಕ = 50 DC 52; a vowel sign goes on C1 and the subjoined form follows: ಕ್ಕಿ = 51 52, ಕ್ಕು = 50 DC E1 52; some subjoined forms fuse with ೃ/ೈ: ಕ್ತೃ = 50 DC F5, ಕ್ತೈ = 50 E6 F4); canonical:halant = code 44 (Unicode virama + ZWNJ: the visible virama glyph 85 replacing the head, ಕ್‌ = 50 85); canonical:tail struck before the reph = accepted, ranked second. preferred: canonical in the main order, then vendor key, then fewer bytes (ಕ್ಷ: the code E1 = FB DC, C + link + ಷ = 50 DC D2; both accepted), then more probes; accepted keeps every canonical spelling. alt:* = the composer answer for another typing order or another visual form (the reph struck before the letter or before the sign; ರ + link + C = ರ with the subjoined C, C3 DC 52, the non-arkavattu form; the lone reph key) - kept, not used as truth. quirk:* = the Unicode composer wrote something other than the codes mean (it drops the length mark 76 after a letter or a cluster, keeps ೢ/ೣ before the link and puts ರ್ after the letter with ೢ/ೣ, drops ಕ್ಷ after the link), or the 7 composer dropped a code the Unicode composer wrote (the pending virama, ZWJ/ZWNJ, the precomposed F0-F3, ೢ ೣ ಌ ॥), a code only the 7 composer types (D7 86 E6 E7 E8 EA EB EE), the nukta before ಿ/ೊ (garbled by the 7 composer), the ಶ್ರೀ code D8 with anything after it, or a lone vowel sign (7 writes the independent vowel glyph) - kept for evidence, not used. Unicode keys are what the Unicode composer wrote, in NFC (ಿ+ೕ = ೀ, ೆ+ೕ = ೇ, ೆ+ೂ = ೊ, ೊ+ೕ = ೋ, ೆ+ೖ = ೈ). Rules with examples: kan7-patterns.txt. Strings a table needs that the composer never spells directly: kan7-composer-gaps.json (derived, not truth).

fontCheck.method: fonts/family-check.json (fontcmp.js + ttf.js): (3,1) cmap of every installed Kannada Shree face - 7: WKAN7001/2.TTF (Shree-Kan7-001/002), S0850890..S0855890 + S0899890 (SHREE-KAN7-0850..0855/0899); 4/5/6: S08500F0..S08550F0 + S08990F0 (SHREE-KAN-0850..0855/0899). Per code: glyph id, advance, sha1 of the glyf bytes.
fontCheck.result: All 16 faces have the same 215 codes on the same code points. SHREE-KAN7-08xx and SHREE-KAN-08xx of the same number are identical code by code (outline bytes and advance, 215/215 for all seven designs). Shree-Kan7-001/002 are other designs with the same code set (glyph ids differ in 164 codes, the order of glyphs in the file, not the code meaning). ONE table serves both families.

counts.notProbed: A conjunct slot holds at most 4 codes and a slot reference inside a slot is ignored, so these are not in the truth: three-consonant clusters C1್C2್C3 (5 codes; their pieces "link C2 link C3" are probed, P set, and C1 + those pieces concatenate); a two-code vowel sign (ೀ = ಿ + 76, ೇ = ೆ + 76, ೋ = ೊ + 76) on a cluster (5 codes; derived in kan7-composer-gaps.json); C1್C2 + sign + tail + reph; reph + C1್C2 + two-code sign.

glyphCheck.swapped9798: ಧಿ family -> 97 (draws ಽ) and ಽ -> 98 (draws ಧಿ) in the composer; 46 truth strings change in the glyphfix file

noGlyphInAnyFace.[ ]: the Unicode composer writes [ ] for codes 28/29, which draw ( ); no face has [ ]
